tasks.title: README.md — document the permission rules init now writes
tasks.description:
Document the new `cairn init` behavior added in task #80.

Add to `README.md` — the Workflow > Initialize section is the natural home, with a cross-reference from Configuration if useful:

1. That `cairn init` offers to write permission rules to `.claude/settings.local.json`, and that the prompt defaults to yes but is skippable.
2. WHAT gets written: read-only git inspection subcommands, allow rules derived from the project's `healthCheck` and `defaultTestCommand`, and deny rules on the five mutating `cairn task` subcommands.
3. WHY: agents that verify a task actually landed — chiefly the post-task reviewer — need to run tests and inspect history. Without these rules a fresh project denies them outright in headless mode.
4. That EXISTING settings are MERGED, not replaced: `permissions.allow` and `permissions.deny` are unioned and every other key is preserved untouched. A user who already has settings from plain `claude` usage will not lose them.
5. That the user should add `.claude/settings.local.json` to their own gitignore — Cairn deliberately does not edit `.gitignore` or global git config, and Claude Code only auto-ignores that file when it writes the file itself.

Keep the existing README structure and table formatting conventions.

CRITICAL GUARD — DO NOT MODIFY `cairn.json`. Its `healthCheck` is pinned to a throwaway outfile and is user-managed for this round. Any disagreement between documentation and `cairn.json`'s current value is EXPECTED — do not reconcile it.
tasks.notes:
# Task #84 — README.md: document the permission rules init now writes

## What changed

Single file touched: `README.md`. Two additions, both cross-referenced.

### 1. Workflow > Initialize (main content, after the existing re-run paragraph)

New paragraph block documenting the `.claude/settings.local.json` seeding
step added by task #80:

1. That `cairn init` offers this (default: yes, skippable) — matches the
   actual prompt copy in `installClaudeSettings()`
   (`src/commands/init.ts:528-533`, `promptBoolean(rl, 'Write permission
   rules?', true)`).
2. WHAT gets written, in an Allow/Deny bullet pair:
   - Allow: the five read-only git inspection subcommands (`diff`, `log`,
     `show`, `status`, `rev-parse` — verified against `GIT_INSPECTION_RULES`
     in `src/claude-settings.ts:71-77`) plus rules derived from
     `healthCheck`/`defaultTestCommand` via `buildCommandRules`.
   - Deny: the five mutating `cairn task` subcommands (`start`, `complete`,
     `set-status`, `add`, `note` — verified against `CAIRN_TASK_DENY_RULES`
     in `src/commands/init.ts:481-487`).
3. WHY: the post-task reviewer (and similar verification agents) run under
   normal permissions, not `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, and need to run
   tests + inspect git history to confirm a task landed — without these
   rules a fresh project denies that outright in headless mode.
4. That existing settings are merged, not replaced — `permissions.allow`
   and `permissions.deny` are unioned, every other key untouched. Matches
   `mergeClaudeSettings()` behavior in `src/claude-settings.ts:229+`
   (`selectNewRules` only adds, existing entries never rewritten).
5. The gitignore note: Cairn deliberately does not touch `.gitignore` or
   global git config; the user must add `.claude/settings.local.json`
   themselves. Matches the WARNING log lines in
   `src/commands/init.ts:559-563` almost verbatim.

### 2. Configuration section cross-reference

One sentence added directly after the `cairn.json` field table, before the
"Health Check Auto-Detection" subheading: notes that `healthCheck` and
`defaultTestCommand` feed the seeded permission rules, with a link back to
`#1-initialize`.

## Verification (facts checked against source, not assumed)

- `src/commands/init.ts:481-566` — read `CAIRN_TASK_DENY_RULES`,
  `buildInitPermissionRules()`, and `installClaudeSettings()` in full;
  matched prompt default, log copy, and gitignore warning text against what
  I wrote.
- `src/claude-settings.ts:71-108, 229-260` — read `GIT_INSPECTION_RULES`,
  `buildCommandRules()`, and `mergeClaudeSettings()` to confirm the exact
  git subcommands and the union/merge (not replace) behavior.
- Existing README table/heading conventions preserved: no structural
  changes, only prose paragraphs and one bullet pair inserted at the
  natural point in the existing Initialize section, plus one sentence in
  Configuration.

## CRITICAL GUARD honored

`cairn.json` was **not** modified by this task. It shows as modified in
`git diff --stat` only because it was already dirty at the start of this
iteration (part of the ongoing self-modifying round's pin — its
`healthCheck` is pointed at a throwaway outfile per the Pin/unpin section
of CLAUDE.md). I only touched `README.md`.

## Tests

`bun run test` → **881 pass, 0 fail** across 30 files, 1772 expect() calls —
identical to the count at the start of this iteration, as expected: this is
a documentation-only change with no source under test. No test added;
README prose has no test harness in this repo, and none was in this task's
declared file scope (`README.md` only).

## Nothing left for the next agent

Documentation is complete and cross-referenced both directions
(Initialize → mentions the settings file; Configuration → links back to
Initialize). No new tasks filed — nothing unrelated surfaced during this
task.
